simple.meaning: הָתַל (hâthal) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to deride ; by implication, to cheat.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 10 times across Genesis, Exodus, Judges, 1 Kings, Job, and 2 more, beginning at Genesis 31:7. Its contexts include family, family line, sacrifice, land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to הָתַל (H2048).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.

occurrences.englishText: Your father has deceived me, and changed my wages ten times, but God didn’t allow him to hurt me.
Pharaoh called for Moses and for Aaron, and said, “Go, sacrifice to your God in the land!”
Delilah said to Samson, “Behold, you have mocked me, and told me lies. Now please tell me how you might be bound.”
Delilah said to Samson, “Until now, you have mocked me and told me lies. Tell me with what you might be bound.”
She said to him, “How can you say, ‘I love you,’ when your heart is not with me? You have mocked me these three times, and have not told me where your great strength lies.”
At noon, Elijah mocked them, and said, “Cry aloud; for he is a god. Either he is deep in thought, or he has gone somewhere, or he is on a journey, or perhaps he sleeps and must be awakened.”
